subject: OptiCart evaluation: success goals, owner stitch, and contract path
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha@opticart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: OptiCart evaluation: success goals, owner stitch, and contract path

Hi Samantha — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Call highlights (short):
- Primary objective: validate Redwood inference latency and cost on OptiCart search reranking (10k qps mix; 128 token average response).
- Success criteria (OptiCart):
  * P95 generation latency < 250ms for T=128 across 99% of test traffic
  * End-to-end query throughput to support peak window of 3k concurrent sessions
  * Cost per 1M tokens under the target shown in the attached quote
  * No outbound data leaving OptiCart VPC during trial (privacy constraint)

Proposed evaluation plan (timeline):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize scope and grant service account + test dataset (anonymized).
- Week 1: Dedicated pilot infra deployed in OptiCart VPC; smoke tests with 1k RPS.
- Week 2: Run production-like workloads, collect latency/cost traces, iterate batching.
- Week 3: Ramp to peak window, produce acceptance report and validation artifacts.
- Week 4: Procurement/contract signature for Dedicated capacity if acceptance gates passed.

Ownership (RACI-style handoff):
- Infra setup: Responsible = Ben Carter (Redwood infra lead)
- App integration / sample harness: Responsible = Marissa Cole (OptiCart eng lead)
- Security & network review: Responsible = Grace O'Connor (Redwood security)
- Account lead / exec sponsor: Accountable = Jordan Blake (Redwood)
- Procurement / commercial signoff: Consult = OptiCart procurement (Samantha + Ruben)

Attachments I uploaded to the thread: trial_scope_v1.pdf (scope), OptiCart_trial_RACI.xlsx (proposed owner matrix), redwood_quote_v1.pdf (initial pricing).

Asks / next steps (actionable):
1) Samantha: confirm procurement contact and target budget window by EOD Thursday.
2) Marissa: share the anonymized test dataset and the service account CIDR for the VPC.
3) Ben: schedule a 60-minute infra kickoff with Marissa/Grace for Wed 09/09; include checklist below.
4) I'll circulate an updated RACI and a short onboarding runbook by EOD tomorrow.

Infra kickoff checklist (short): IAM roles, KMS key access, Egress rules (deny), monitoring hooks, test harness endpoint.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0194

Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 12:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: OptiCart evaluation: success goals, owner stitch, and contract path

Thanks Jordan — good recap. Quick answers:
- Procurement contact = Ruben Torres (cc'd). He manages vendor engagement and budgets.
- Budget band: we're targeting a mid-Q4 procurement, want to keep pilot under $40k list for an initial month.
- Data: I'll share an anonymized sample dataset and the VPC peering CIDR by EOD Wednesday.

Can you confirm whether Redwood needs a dedicated NAT or if you can run entirely inside our VPC (no egress)? We need no outgoing internet calls for compliance.

Also — can you include a short acceptance checklist for our legal team to review (data handling, logs retention, SOC 2 reference)? If you can attach that to the runbook that would speed review.

Best,
Samantha Liu
VP Product, OptiCart
Samantha.Liu@opticart.com

Thanks — flagged a couple infra items for the kickoff:
- We can run fully in OptiCart VPC using customer-hosted gateways. No outbound egress required; we'll bring the inference runtime into the VPC and use private endpoints for telemetry (push over a secure tunnel to your monitoring collector).
- Capacity note: to hit 3k concurrent sessions with T=128 we'll need 4x A100-equivalent slots for the pilot; I'll provide an optimized batching config that should reduce that by ~30% in most workloads.
- KMS: need a key ARN and a service account with decrypt permissions for model artifacts.

I've attached a short infra checklist in the shared drive link (will paste to the runbook).

Ben Carter
Head of Serving | Redwood Inference
